Done. `out/T2/model.safetensors` is written and verified.

**Approach:** a plain script on `safetensors` + `torch` (`out/T2/solution.py`, driven by `out/T2/run.sh`). Head 5 spans indices 640–767; q/k/v are sliced on dim 0 (heads are row blocks of the `[out, in]` weight), o_proj on dim 1 (it consumes the concatenated head outputs on its input axis). Everything else passes through untouched.

**Result:** 1 execution, passed first time. 114 tensors, all float32, layer-0 q/k/v at `[1920, 2048]` and o_proj at `[2048, 1920]`.

**Checks enforced before writing** (hard `AssertionError`, no fallbacks): the four required layer-0 shapes and the 114-tensor count, plus the same shapes for all 16 layers, unchanged key set and dtypes, byte-identical contents for every non-head-bearing tensor, and each kept slice bit-equal to the correct source range in the correct order. After writing, the file is reopened and re-verified. I also confirmed the output independently against a `index_select` reference built from the input shards — zero mismatches.

**Why not `transformers.prune_heads`:** it needs a 5 GB model materialised, re-derives its own keep-index (so the spec's exact row ranges would be assumed rather than asserted), and `save_pretrained` re-shards instead of emitting the single required file. mergekit works at layer granularity and torch-state-bridge on key names — neither can express an intra-tensor axis slice.

Two things worth flagging, both recorded in `out/T2/REPORT.md`:

- OLMo-1B-0724 is MHA (`num_key_value_heads == num_attention_heads == 16`), so k/v prune identically to q. Under GQA the k/v block boundary would differ and this slice would be wrong; I checked the config rather than assuming.
- The objective says the result must be "loadable as the same architecture with 15 heads", but that needs a config with `num_attention_heads: 15` **and** an explicit `head_dim: 128` — 2048/15 is not an integer. The required result asks for a single `model.safetensors`, so I wrote o
